title: Epic
doel: Define a deliverable block of business value that enables traceability and budget control.
note: Sign-off is formal when the epic has budget impact. For smaller initiatives, informal PO agreement suffices.
template:
# Epic: [Name]

## Business Outcome

## Problem Statement

## Target Users

## Success Metrics (KPIs)
| Metric | Baseline | Target | Measurement |
|---|---|---|---|

## Scope
### In Scope

### Out of Scope

## Features
| Feature | Priority | Status |
|---|---|---|

## Assumptions

## Dependencies

## Open Questions

aiTasks.name: Business Value Validator
aiTasks.objective: Validate the epic has a clear, measurable outcome with realistic KPIs.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Product Owner. Review this epic: (1) Is business outcome measurable? (2) Are KPIs SMART? (3) Is scope realistic? (4) Are dependencies identified? Output PASS/WARN/FAIL per criterion.

aiTasks.name: Feature Decomposer
aiTasks.objective: Break the epic into logical features with clear boundaries.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Senior BA. Suggest a feature breakdown: (1) full scope coverage, (2) clear boundaries, (3) independently deliverable, (4) logically sequenced. For each: one-sentence description and inter-feature dependencies.

aiTasks.name: Spike Planner
aiTasks.objective: Identify technical uncertainties in this epic that need a spike before writing feature specs.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Solution Architect. Review this epic for technical uncertainties that should be explored via a spike before writing feature specs: (1) Unclear implementation approach, (2) New or unfamiliar technology, (3) Performance unknowns, (4) Integration unknowns. For each: name it, estimate risk (H/M/L), propose a spike question, suggest a timebox. Output as a spike candidate list.

aiTasks.name: Epic Scope Diagram
aiTasks.objective: Generate a mindmap of epic scope only if the epic spans 4+ features or has a non-obvious decomposition.
aiTasks.prompt:
Assess first: only generate a diagram if this document has structural complexity that text alone would obscure — multiple decision points, 4+ interacting actors, entity relationships, or parallel paths. If the content is simple or linear, reply: **"No diagram needed — the text is sufficient."**

If a diagram IS warranted, generate valid Mermaid syntax.

You are a Solution Architect decomposing an epic.

Assessment: Does this epic contain 4 or more distinct features or capability areas? Is the decomposition non-obvious (i.e., not just a simple list)? If the scope is simple, a diagram adds no clarity.

If warranted, generate a `mindmap` with:
- Root: epic name
- Level 1: capability areas or themes
- Level 2: features or deliverables under each area
- Max 3 levels deep

Output only the mermaid code block, no explanation.

title: Feature
sub: Scoped piece of functionality within an epic
lifecycle: Living — updated on refinement or scope changes
doel: Document behaviour and business rules per functional block as the basis for stories and technical design.
template:
# Feature: [Name]

Epic: [link]

## Description

## User Goals

## Business Rules
| # | Rule | Example |
|---|---|---|

## State Machine
| State | Trigger | Next State | Actor |
|---|---|---|---|

## Acceptance Criteria (summary)

## Out of Scope

## Open Questions

## Change Log
| Date | Change | Author |
|---|---|---|

## Traceability Matrix
| Story | AC | Task | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| US-001 | AC-001 | T-01 | TC-01 |

aiTasks.name: Business Rules Extractor
aiTasks.objective: Surface implicit business rules assumed but not yet documented.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Senior BA. Read this feature and identify implicit business rules. Write each as: "IF [condition] THEN [result]". Flag rules that conflict with each other. Output: original assumption | explicit rule | conflict risk.

aiTasks.name: Complexity Estimator
aiTasks.objective: Assess technical complexity and surface implementation risks.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Tech Lead. Assess this feature: (1) complexity H/M/L with justification, (2) key implementation risks, (3) architectural decisions required, (4) estimated story count. Flag anything needing clarification before stories are written.

aiTasks.name: Clarification Generator
aiTasks.objective: Surface ambiguities in this feature and generate structured options for stakeholder resolution.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Business Analyst. Review this feature for ambiguities: (1) Terms with multiple valid interpretations, (2) Business rules that conflict or overlap, (3) Scenarios not covered by ACs, (4) Assumptions stated as facts. For each: write the clarification question, then 2-3 concrete options with trade-offs pre-filled so the stakeholder only needs to choose. Format as CLR-NNN entries ready for the Clarification Log.

aiTasks.name: Feature State Diagram
aiTasks.objective: Generate a state or flow diagram for this feature only if it involves a lifecycle with multiple states or a non-trivial decision flow.
aiTasks.prompt:
Assess first: only generate a diagram if this document has structural complexity that text alone would obscure — multiple decision points, 4+ interacting actors, entity relationships, or parallel paths. If the content is simple or linear, reply: **"No diagram needed — the text is sufficient."**

If a diagram IS warranted, generate valid Mermaid syntax.

You are a Solution Architect analysing a feature.

Assessment: Does this feature involve an entity with 4+ lifecycle states, or a user flow with branching decisions? Simple CRUD features or single-path flows do not warrant a diagram.

If warranted, choose the correct type:
- Use `stateDiagram-v2` if the feature has an entity with a meaningful lifecycle (draft → review → approved → archived, etc.)
- Use `flowchart TD` if it is a decision-heavy process (multiple conditions determining next steps)

Include: all states/steps, transitions with labels, and error/exception paths.

Output only the mermaid code block, no explanation.

title: User Story
doel: Define one testable piece of user value. Acceptance criteria live in a separate ac.md file.
outputs: Linked to ac.md for acceptance criteria
note: Acceptance Criteria are maintained in a separate ac.md file alongside story.md. This improves AI processing and keeps each file focused.
template:
# User Story: US-XXX-NNN [Name]

**As a** [role],
**I want to** [action],
**so that** [value].

Feature: [link]
Status: draft / in review / approved / in sprint / done
Points: ?

## Open Questions
| ID | Question | Options | Resolution | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q-01 | | A: ... / B: ... | Pending | |

## Out of Scope

## Notes

## Linked Documents
- Acceptance Criteria: ac.md
- NFR: nfr.md (if applicable)

aiTasks.name: INVEST Validator
aiTasks.objective: Validate the story meets INVEST criteria (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable).
aiTasks.prompt: You are an Agile Coach. Validate this user story against INVEST: (1) Independent — can it be delivered without other stories? (2) Negotiable — is the scope flexible? (3) Valuable — clear user value? (4) Estimable — enough detail to estimate? (5) Small — fits in one sprint? (6) Testable — can it be verified? Output PASS/WARN/FAIL per criterion.

aiTasks.name: Story Splitter
aiTasks.objective: Split the story into smaller sub-stories if it is too large for a single sprint.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Senior BA. Assess if this user story is too large for one sprint. If yes, suggest 2-3 smaller sub-stories using valid splitting patterns (by workflow step, business rule, user role, data type, CRUD operation, happy path first). Each sub-story must be independently deliverable.

aiTasks.name: Clarification Generator
aiTasks.objective: Surface ambiguities in this story before refinement.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Business Analyst. Review this user story for ambiguities before refinement: (1) Is the user role specific enough? (2) Is the action clear enough to test? (3) Is the value measurable? (4) Are there implicit business rules not stated? For each: write the question with 2-3 options + trade-offs. Format as Q-NNN entries for the Open Questions section.

aiTasks.name: Story Flow Diagram
aiTasks.objective: Generate a flow diagram only if this story involves a multi-step interaction or conditional logic that prose cannot make unambiguous.
aiTasks.prompt:
Assess first: only generate a diagram if this document has structural complexity that text alone would obscure — multiple decision points, 4+ interacting actors, entity relationships, or parallel paths. If the content is simple or linear, reply: **"No diagram needed — the text is sufficient."**

If a diagram IS warranted, generate valid Mermaid syntax.

You are a BA reviewing a user story.

Assessment: Does this story involve 3+ sequential steps with conditional branches, or interactions between 2+ systems? Single-action stories ("as a user I want to see X") never need a diagram.

If warranted, generate a `sequenceDiagram` or `flowchart TD`:
- Use `sequenceDiagram` if there is an interaction between user + frontend + backend + database
- Use `flowchart TD` if it is purely a decision flow within one system

Keep to the happy path + one exception path maximum.

Output only the mermaid code block, no explanation.

title: Acceptance Criteria
lifecycle: One-time — closed with the story after sprint review
doel: Define all testable conditions for accepting a story as done, separated from the story definition for clarity and AI processing efficiency.
outputs: Verifiable acceptance criteria in EARS format

substeps.name: Add edge cases and error scenarios

note: EARS notation: WHEN [condition] THE [actor] SHALL [observable behaviour]. Keep each AC independently verifiable.
template:
# Acceptance Criteria: [Story Name] (US-XXX-NNN)

Story: [link to story.md]
Feature: [link]
Status: draft / approved

## Happy Path

### AC-001: [Short name]
WHEN [condition]
THE [actor] SHALL [observable behaviour]

## Edge Cases

### EC-001: [Short name]
WHEN [condition]
THE [actor] SHALL [observable behaviour]

## Error Scenarios

### AC-002: [Short name]
WHEN [condition]
THE [actor] SHALL [observable behaviour]

## Compliance Checklist
- [ ] GDPR: Does this feature process personal data?
  - [ ] Consent mechanism in place
  - [ ] Data retention period defined
  - [ ] Deletion pathway documented
- [ ] Auth: All sensitive operations require authenticated session
- [ ] Logging: No PII written to logs
- [ ] Encryption: Sensitive data encrypted at rest and in transit

## Notes

aiTasks.name: AC Generator
aiTasks.objective: Generate complete EARS-format ACs covering happy path, edge cases, and error scenarios.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a QA Engineer expert in EARS notation (WHEN [condition] THE [actor] SHALL [observable behaviour]). Based on this story and feature, generate: (1) happy path ACs, (2) edge case ACs (boundaries, empty states, max values), (3) error scenario ACs (invalid input, auth failures, system errors). Each AC must be independently testable.

aiTasks.name: Edge Case Detective
aiTasks.objective: Identify security, permission, and boundary edge cases the BA likely missed.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Security Engineer reviewing requirements. Identify: (1) authorisation edge cases (unauthorised data access), (2) input validation gaps (injection, XSS, oversized input), (3) concurrency issues (race conditions, simultaneous submits), (4) state edge cases (unexpected object states). Output as "What if..." scenarios, each a candidate AC.
